summary.oneLiner: Azad is a globally-qualified single/limited-source supplier of the hardest-to-make rotating + hot-section turbine and aero/defence components, competing head-on with US/EU/China/Japan incumbents on the same OEM platforms. Reported growth is the conversion of multi-year qualifications against ~70-80% complete capacity build-out, not a short-term tailwind. INR6,500cr+ rolling order book (~11-12x FY26 revenue) gives multi-year 25%+ revenue visibility with structurally high (~37%) EBITDA margins.

thesis: Azad is a globally-qualified single/limited-source supplier of the hardest-to-make rotating + hot-section turbine and aero/defence components, competing head-on with US/EU/China/Japan incumbents on the same OEM platforms. scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | FY26 | FY25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR157cr | (+26.4% YoY) | INR590cr (standalone) / INR603cr (consol) | INR453cr |
| Revenue growth | +26.4% YoY | — | ~30%+ (32%+ consol) | — |
| EBITDA margin (reported) | 36.7% | 36.5% | 36.9% (std) / 37.4% (consol) | — |
| PAT margin | 22.3% | 20.9% | 22.4% | — |
| PAT | — | — | INR132cr (std) / INR134cr (consol), +54.4% | — |
| Energy & O&G seg | INR128cr (~81% of qtr) | — | INR481cr (~81.5%, +34%) | — |
| A&D segment | INR28cr | — | INR101cr (~17.2%, +25%) — first INR100cr+ year | — |
guidance:
- Top-line ~25%+ growth reaffirmed for FY27 AND on a multi-year basis (next ~5 years to consume the ~INR6,500cr book).
- Mgmt repeatedly flagged 25% as conservative; expects to revise upward once new plants stabilize 100% (currently 70-80%). "Some movement of revenues" expected from Q1 FY27 ("churnout" quarter).
- Margin band guided 33-35%+ with the "+" being upside; mgmt hopeful of beating it via continuous improvement.
- Working capital: receivable days to fall toward ~200 days in H1 FY27, ~160-170 days in H2 FY27.
order book:
- Rolling order book ~INR6,500cr+ (net of ~INR600cr delivered in FY26), ~11-12x FY26 revenue; some added contracts not disclosable.
- Segment split (USD): Energy >$400m · Aerospace & Defence >$200m · Oil & Gas >$100m.
- Average contract tenure 5-6 years; conversion driven by (1) agreed production schedules, (2) capacity ramp, (3) per-part qualification status — all three "aligned for the first time at scale."
- New marquee win: MHI Japan single-source 8-year contract for hot-section Nozzle Vane segments (gas-turbine combustion). Strong endorsement; only ~3 players globally (vs Howmet, PCC).
segment:
- **Energy & Oil & Gas** ~81% of revenue; gas + steam + nuclear turbines. Nuclear: qualified supplier to EDF/Arabelle Solutions (France), one of few qualified nuclear-turbine-airfoil makers in India.
- **Oil & Gas**: still largely under qualification; <INR10cr FY26; Baker Hughes the only customer; dedicated facility inaugurated Apr 2026; FY27 = first ramp year.
- **Aerospace & Defence** ~17% of revenue; crossed INR100cr first time; airfoils for 4 engine OEMs — Rolls-Royce first (first qualification batch H2 FY27, supply momentum Q4 FY27/early FY28), then Pratt & Whitney, then Safran. ATGG indigenous defence engine ("years → months → weeks" to delivery).
- 5-yr mix target: Energy ~55-60%, balance A&D + O&G (deliberate diversification from 2020 single-product compressor-airfoil energy business).
growth: Three levers: (1) rising wallet/market share on already-qualified parts (bulk of current growth — the 25% guide is on qualified products only, excludes future qualifications/engine/hot-section upside); (2) adding adjacent categories/part numbers (e.g., MHI hot-section — higher entry barrier, higher asset turn); (3) horizontal deployment of capabilities to new customers across the 3-4-player oligopoly structure of each end market.
margins:
- FY26 reported EBITDA 36.9% std / 37.4% consol despite new plants underutilized; margin aided by backward integration (lower outsourcing), supply-chain efficiency, scale, mix.
- Operating leverage from the 4 new plants still ahead → potential further upside ("margin surprise" flagged by analyst, mgmt non-committal but optimistic).
- Other income INR46cr FY26 (FX gain + treasury) expected to moderate as QIP proceeds deployed to capex.
- MHI hot-section likely above blended margin band (mgmt declined specifics; pointed to public margins of Howmet/PCC as a read).
capex:
- FY26 capitalized assets INR392cr; CWIP + capital advances +INR191cr.
- Infrastructure build-out ~70-80% complete; heaviest spend behind.
- Capex linked to INR700cr QIP; ~INR180-190cr balance QIP deployment still to come.
- 8-plant program: 4 dedicated lean facilities done (GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi, Baker Hughes), balance 4 to be completed within FY27. Third large 85,000 sqm plant deferred — civil work to start only after current/balance plants ramp.
- Saudi Arabia / Baker Hughes plant: still on but timelines shifted; deprioritized vs current capacity ramp.
- Special processes being insourced: vacuum heat treatment + NADCAP-approved heat treatment, shot peening, coatings already in-house; remaining few to follow.
capital allocation:
- QIP INR700cr raised; ~INR160cr of QIP within INR184cr treasury balance.
- Net debt INR272cr (gross borrowing INR457cr); incremental term funding INR154cr in FY26 for capacity.
- GST credit ~INR100cr accumulated (capex-driven), expected realized by H1 FY28 → liquidity tailwind.
- Receivables INR309cr; payables INR87cr (~51 days); ~96% inventory <1yr old (ramp/qualification/stocking driven, not legacy).
- Priority: deploy capex into capacity, then normalize working capital and convert inventory to revenue/cash from FY27.
risks:
- Execution/ramp risk acknowledged as the residual risk (demand, capacity, manpower largely de-risked via multi-year contracts and qualifications).
- Elevated working capital / inventory build; cash-flow conversion dependent on plant utilization ramping FY27+.
- Front-ended depreciation & finance costs rising from heavy FY26 capex.
- Long, costly qualification cycles (years) gate new-program revenue (e.g., R-R supply only Q4 FY27/FY28).
- Middle East geopolitics: viewed as a macro risk, "business as usual"; Saudi plant timeline shifted due to regional situation.
- Organizational restructuring — selectively replacing functional leaders outgrown by scale (key-person/transition risk).
mgmt tone: Confident and deliberate; emphasis on "calibrated, not rushed" execution and conservatism (guidance on qualified products only). Repeated signalling that the 25% guide understates true potential and may be revised up after stabilization. Transparent on working-capital pain; guarded on defence (ATGG) and hot-section contract specifics, repeatedly inviting analysts for plant visits.
non-obvious:
- MHI hot-section nozzle vanes were previously made in-house by MHI — now single-sourced to Azad; positions Azad directly against Howmet/PCC in a ~3-player global niche.
- The 25%+ guidance explicitly excludes ATGG engine, hot-section ramp, and all yet-to-qualify programs — pure upside optionality.
- ATGG defence engine moving from current 3.7-4 kiloton thrust class toward higher-capacity engines and larger programs (indigenization read-through).
- Nuclear is an existing, already-qualified revenue stream (EDF/Arabelle), not just a theme — rare qualified nuclear-turbine-airfoil capability in India.
- ~96% inventory <1yr old reframes the "elevated inventory" optics as forward-stocking, not obsolescence.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge / theme | Direction | Name | NSE | BSE | Role | Conviction | Coverage | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualification-led conversion of INR6,500cr book + 25%+ multi-year growth | beneficiary | Azad Engineering | AZAD | 544061 | Self | High | self | Capacity, qualifications, schedules aligned at scale |
| MHI single-source hot-section nozzle vanes; entering global ~3-player niche | loser | Howmet Aerospace | — | (code unverified) | Incumbent global hot-section supplier | Med | external | Azad enters their turf as new qualified player |
| Same as above | loser | Precision Castparts (PCC) | — | (code unverified) | Incumbent global precision-cast/hot-section supplier | Med | external | Now a Berkshire subsidiary; faces new Indian competitor |
| Gas-turbine demand ramp (power/data-center) | beneficiary | Mitsubishi Heavy Industries | — | (code unverified) | OEM customer awarding 8-yr single-source | Med | external | Secures critical hot-section supply via Azad |
| Energy/power-gen ramp | beneficiary | GE / Siemens | — | (code unverified) | OEM customers, dedicated Azad facilities | Med | external | Capacity dedicated to their platforms |
| Oil & Gas precision components ramp | beneficiary | Baker Hughes | — | (code unverified) | OEM customer, dedicated facility (Apr-26) | Med | external | FY27 first ramp year for O&G segment |
| Nuclear turbine resurgence | beneficiary | EDF / Arabelle Solutions | — | (code unverified) | Nuclear-turbine OEM customer (France) | Med | external | Azad qualified nuclear-airfoil supplier |
| Aero-engine airfoil qualifications (multi-year) | beneficiary | Rolls-Royce / Pratt & Whitney / Safran | — | (code unverified) | Aero-engine OEM customers in qualification | Low | external | Supply only from Q4 FY27/FY28 onward |
| Indigenous defence engine (ATGG) | beneficiary | Azad Engineering | AZAD | 544061 | Self — national defence program supplier | Med | self | Delivery imminent ("weeks"); specifics undisclosed |
qoq change log:
- vs prior quarter (Q3 FY26): Order book held at ~INR6,500cr+ (rolling, net of ~INR600cr FY26 deliveries); analyst attempt to gross-up to ~INR8,500cr corrected by mgmt.
- New since last call: MHI Japan 8-year single-source hot-section nozzle-vane contract; Baker Hughes dedicated facility inaugurated Apr 2026 (4th dedicated facility since listing, 2 commissioned in FY26).
- Build-out progress: infrastructure now ~70-80% complete; 4 of 8 dedicated plants done, balance 4 within FY27.
- Working-capital guidance refined: receivable days target ~200 (H1 FY27) → ~160-170 (H2 FY27).
- Margin: full-year reported EBITDA 36.9% std / 37.4% consol; Q4 PAT margin up to 22.3% (from 20.9% YoY).
- Guidance reaffirmed 25%+ (FY27 and multi-year), mgmt flags upside bias post-stabilization.

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Preferred name in manufacturing of highly-engineered, complex and mission & life-critical components, with ~1,700+ qualified parts and components, 45+ qualified manufacturing processes and 15+ years in operations as a Tier 1 supplier.
- Components supplier to six of the key manufacturers in aerospace & defence and to five of the key manufacturers in the turbine manufacturing industry; supplier to customers which control c. 75% of the gas turbine market globally (deck note: based on orders in H2FY25).
- Entry barriers cited at each stage: stringent vendor qualification taking 30-48 months, a separate qualification process for each component, zero parts per million defect requirements, and substantial upfront capital.
- 3.82mn units of parts delivered between FY09 and FY26, some with zero parts per million defect requirement; sales in 12 countries with ~93% export revenue in FY26 and 96%+ of revenue from private players.
- End-markets sized by the deck at CY29 TAM of INR 2,190 bn (Aerospace & Defence), INR 930 bn (Oil & Gas) and INR 310 bn (Energy); the A&D addressable market is shown growing from Rs 1,190 bn in 2023 to Rs 2,190 bn in 2029 (+11%).

| Challenge / theme | Direction | Name | Role | Conviction | Coverage | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualification-led conversion of INR6,500cr book + 25%+ multi-year growth | beneficiary | Azad Engineering (AZAD) | Self | High | self | Capacity, qualifications, schedules aligned at scale |
| MHI single-source hot-section nozzle vanes; entering global ~3-player niche | loser | Howmet Aerospace | Incumbent global hot-section supplier | Med | external | Azad enters their turf as new qualified player |
| Same as above | loser | Precision Castparts (PCC) | Incumbent global precision-cast/hot-section supplier | Med | external | Now a Berkshire subsidiary; faces new Indian competitor |
| Gas-turbine demand ramp (power/data-center) | beneficiary | Mitsubishi Heavy Industries | OEM customer awarding 8-yr single-source | Med | external | Secures critical hot-section supply via Azad |
| Energy/power-gen ramp | beneficiary | GE / Siemens | OEM customers, dedicated Azad facilities | Med | external | Capacity dedicated to their platforms |
| Oil & Gas precision components ramp | beneficiary | Baker Hughes | OEM customer, dedicated facility (Apr-26) | Med | external | FY27 first ramp year for O&G segment |
| Nuclear turbine resurgence | beneficiary | EDF / Arabelle Solutions | Nuclear-turbine OEM customer (France) | Med | external | Azad qualified nuclear-airfoil supplier |
| Aero-engine airfoil qualifications (multi-year) | beneficiary | Rolls-Royce / Pratt & Whitney / Safran | Aero-engine OEM customers in qualification | Low | external | Supply only from Q4 FY27/FY28 onward |
| Indigenous defence engine (ATGG) | beneficiary | Azad Engineering (AZAD) | Self — national defence program supplier | Med | self | Delivery imminent ("weeks"); specifics undisclosed |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- vs prior quarter (Q3 FY26): Order book held at ~INR6,500cr+ (rolling, net of ~INR600cr FY26 deliveries); analyst attempt to gross-up to ~INR8,500cr corrected by mgmt.
- New since last call: MHI Japan 8-year single-source hot-section nozzle-vane contract; Baker Hughes dedicated facility inaugurated Apr 2026 (4th dedicated facility since listing, 2 commissioned in FY26).
- Build-out progress: infrastructure now ~70-80% complete; 4 of 8 dedicated plants done, balance 4 within FY27.
- Working-capital guidance refined: receivable days target ~200 (H1 FY27) → ~160-170 (H2 FY27).
- Margin: full-year reported EBITDA 36.9% std / 37.4% consol; Q4 PAT margin up to 22.3% (from 20.9% YoY).
- Guidance reaffirmed 25%+ (FY27 and multi-year), mgmt flags upside bias post-stabilization.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Milestone] Azad delivered its first expendable indigenous turbojet engine to DRDO and the Ministry of Defence - designed by GTRE and manufactured & assembled by Azad - which the deck calls a pivotal step from component manufacturer to propulsion systems player.
- [Order wins - self-identified] Purchase order from BHEL for advanced, high-complex rotating airfoils for supercritical turbines under an indigenization project evaluated and approved by the Central Electricity Authority Ministry of Power, NTPC and BHEL; a Honeywell Aerospace ISC (USA) business award with Phase 1 valued at USD 16 Mn; an LTCPA with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries valued at USD 83 Mn for 5 years; and an additional strategic supply agreement with Nuovo Pignone srl of Baker Hughes, amended for five years expiring in CY 2030.
- [Order wins - counterparty binding lost in extraction] The orders slides also list contracts valued at USD 112 Mn (rotating and stationary airfoils for advanced gas turbine engines), USD 90 Mn (combustion commodities, cold blades and machined parts), USD 53.5 Mn (airfoils for advanced nuclear, industrial and thermal power), USD 40 Mn (critical and highly complex rotating and stationary components) and an 8-year single-source LTCPA for hot-section nozzle vane segments; each slide carries five customer names against seven paragraphs, so these are not attributed to a specific customer here.
- [Guidance] Supported by a strong order book, the company reiterates its long-term revenue growth guidance of over 25%.
- [Saudi Arabia] An MoU has been signed to set up a facility to manufacture and supply precision components, sub-assemblies and assemblies to cater to requirements within the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
